item.title: n8n LangChain RAG Tutorial: Build a Chatbot That Answers from Your Documents (2026)
item.description:
Introduction

A chatbot that answers from your own documents beats a generic chatbot for one reason: it stops hallucinating about your content. This tutorial builds a complete retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline in n8n, from raw documents to a working chat interface. You will run Qdrant in Docker, ingest documents with n8n’s LangChain nodes, and serve answers through a Chat Trigger. It is written for n8n users who are comfortable building basic workflows and want their first real AI feature, and every node name below was verified in a lab install of n8n 2.41.4.

item.title: n8n vs Make for AI Agents: Which One Should You Build On?
item.description:
Introduction

If you’re picking a platform to build AI agents in 2026, n8n and Make are the two serious contenders outside the pure-code world. Both let you give a language model tools, memory, and a job to do, but they charge differently, architect agents differently, and suit different teams. This guide compares them on the dimensions that actually decide the choice: agent architecture, model freedom, memory and knowledge, the real cost math for agent workloads, and who should pick which. The n8n side below is grounded in a build I verified on n8n 2.40.7 (see our full n8n AI agent tutorial); the Make side follows Make’s official AI Agents documentation.
